title: 27 Sep 2026 grade recheck of the 2.34 1.17 strategy review
requested_by: owner, 27 Sep 2026 (scheduled recheck reminder, answered yes)
scope: 21 grades flagged by the 2.34 review, added on 25 Sep, or withheld by the engine for "Statistics moved since review", plus a proposed (not applied) first grade for Baron Valmont midlane. The other 63 grades, hero notes other than the five role notes and the summary note, counters, adaptations, compositions and plans were not re-reviewed.
standard: re-examined the 21 grades the review flagged or the engine withheld against about five days of the whole 1.17 line (1.17 plus Hotfix 1.17.1). It kept the review's standard (a kit or patch reason with evidence pointing the same way; a high rate alone never raises a grade), and added one rule: a grade may drop one step without a kit reason when the whole-line 95% interval excludes the previous-patch review rate with at least 500 games and the games since the review point the same way. Rechecked entries show their own date and cite the rechecked sample.

entries.why: Mercy and repeated attacks build Vengeance before Dusk; Shadow Glide offers a way to preserve space or follow a confirmed catch.
entries.watch: 1.17 raised Mercy damage and Dusk now refunds mana on a kill, and her results since the review have risen with them. Purge is an exposed commitment that still needs control or peel, and the refund needs a kill.
entries.reason: B to A. Kit reason: 1.17 raised Mercy base damage from 20/25/30/35/40 to 25/30/35/40/45 and physical power growth from 3.5 to 3.7 (base 54 to 53), and Dusk refunds 35% of its mana when it kills. At review the early evidence pointed the other way (45.1% over 412, 95% 40.4-50.0). It now agrees: the whole 1.17 line (1.17 plus Hotfix 1.17.1) is 50.9% over 1266 [48.2, 53.7], above the 1.16.4 review sample (48.6% over 5474), and the 854 games since the review ran 53.7% (two-proportion z about 2.9 against the review sample). The interval still includes 48.6%, so, as with Murdock's 2.34 raise, the move rests on the buffs with evidence consistent in direction. One step: A (strong alternative with a clear role) fits a follow-up carry; she stays below the S carries. Bronze+ 50.6% over 2431 is nested, not independent.
entries.limitation: The rise is concentrated in the days after the review; early-patch learning on a buffed hero is a plausible part of it. Her other roles are too small to use.

entries.why: Saturation Charge and Orbital Sanction offer area pressure alongside ranged attacks; the Scorched Earth plan adds napalm zones where mines, Frag Order and the beam land.
entries.watch: 1.17 widened the rifle projectile, but his 1.17 carry results stayed near even, below the S carries. The ability-oriented plan converts an allied catch, and bonus attack speed becomes haste, not firing speed.
entries.reason: S to A. The 2.34 review named him the S carry most worth rechecking (48.6% over 529, 95% 44.4-52.8, against the 1.16.4 review sample 52.6% over 6656). The whole 1.17 line is 49.8% over 1623 [47.4, 52.2], an interval that now excludes the 1.16.4 rate, and the 1094 games since the review ran 50.4%, the same direction. His only 1.17 change, a 10% larger rifle hitbox, helps consistency but adds no damage, so nothing in the patch argues for keeping S. He is the lowest S carry (Drongo 52.2%, Eden 52.3%, Sparrow 51.4%) and below the A Revenant (54.1%). One step: his area-pressure job and the Scorched Earth plan are intact. Bronze+ 51.3% over 4235 is nested and higher.
entries.limitation: No kit change points down; the move rests on a larger sample confirming the early drop (the recheck's rule for a downward move without a kit reason). Bronze+ is higher. The hitbox effect on hit rate is unmeasured.

entries.why: Cosmic Rift supports lane pressure while Torn Space preserves positioning; Black Hole offers a clear conversion for jungle or support control.
entries.watch: 1.17 trimmed Void Breach, Black Hole, Event Horizon and his mana scaling, and Hotfix 1.17.1 removed a Black Hole bug that favored him, so he is an A conversion pick for a coordinated team. A Ground effect now stops Torn Space, and interrupts land once the Truesilver shield breaks.
entries.reason: S to A. Kit reason: the 1.17 cuts (Cosmic Power 1% bonus max mana per 15 to per 20 magical power; Void Breach 100-260 to 90-250 and its cooldown scaling per 80 to per 100 max mana; Black Hole 520/780/1040 to 500/760/1020; Event Horizon 5% to 4%) plus Hotfix 1.17.1, which stopped Black Hole pulling enemies when its cast was interrupted, a bug that favored him. At review the evidence did not agree (51.6% over 595 against the 1.16.4 rate of 51.2% over 9581). It now does: the whole 1.17 line is 49.4% over 1739 [47.1, 51.7], and the 1144 games since the review ran 48.3%. Pred.gg lists the hotfix build from 24 Sep 10:00 UTC, about 7.5 hours after the review sample was collected, so nearly all of those games are after the fix. The interval still includes 51.2%, so the move rests on the kit and hotfix with evidence consistent in direction, the standard that moved Morigesh and Murdock in 2.34. Bronze+ 48.8% over 4121 is nested and agrees.
entries.limitation: The Pred.gg sample pools versions 167 and 168; the before/after-hotfix split is inferred from collection times, not queried per version. His Black Hole composition role is unchanged.

entries.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained lane pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.
entries.watch: 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth, and his 1.17 offlane results sit near even, so he is a strong lane-pressure option rather than the default. Buy real defense on time; personal survival is not allied peel, and the draft still needs a reliable catch.
entries.reason: S to A. Kit reason: official 1.17 base health 690 to 680 and armor growth 5.4 to 4.8. The evidence now points the same way: the whole 1.17 line is 50.3% over 1884 [48.0, 52.5], which excludes the 1.16.4 review rate (53.3% over 8824), and the 1248 games since the review ran 49.5%. At review the interval (47.9-55.6 over 636) still included 53.3%, so the nerf alone did not move him. A kit reason with evidence pointing the same way is the review's main standard (it moved Serath S to A). Bronze+ 52.3% over 4665 is nested and higher.
entries.limitation: Close call. The 2.34 limitation named 'a larger 1.17 sample below 50%' as the trigger; he is just above it (50.3%), and Bronze+ is higher. The move rests on the main standard, not on that trigger. The lane-pressure job is unchanged.

entries.why: Static Trap and Buckshot can buy firing space, while Long Arm of the Law converts a distant catch without abandoning the lane.
entries.watch: 1.17 raised Shots Fired, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law damage, but his 1.17 carry results fell below his previous patch, so he is a comfort or matchup pick. Save Buckshot and traps for the diver.
entries.reason: B back to C. The 2.34 raise rested on the three 1.17 buffs plus early results consistent in direction (47.9% over 541 against 46.2% over 5224 on 1.16.4). The second part has reversed: the whole 1.17 line is 44.4% over 1579 [42.0, 46.9], below his 1.16.4 rate, and the 1038 games since the review ran 42.6% (z about -2.0 against the review sample). A raise whose evidence no longer points the same way does not meet the standard, so the grade returns to the pre-review C. He is now the lowest carry (Skylar 45.5%, TwinBlast 48.8%). The interval still includes the 1.16.4 rate, so this reverses the raise; it is not a further drop. Bronze+ 47.0% over 3280 is nested and higher.
entries.limitation: The buffs are real and nothing in 1.17 explains the fall. It may reflect who picked him up after the buffs, which the data cannot separate.

entries.why: Arterial Grip grounds and slows a bound target so Rupture and Bloodbound can land, and Exsanguinate's bats return health, far more when they hit heroes. The grounding bind also stops dashes such as Torn Space.
entries.watch: No dash: crowd control on Valmont, broken line of sight or distance breaks the bind, and Exsanguinate costs more mana each second it stays on, so toggle it off between fights. His Gold+ midlane results sit near even, so treat him as a practiced pick.
entries.reason: New entry. 2.34 left him ungraded (44.1% over 354 Gold+ games after 1.5 days, heavily banned). Hotfix 1.17.1 fixed Sanguine Banquet's incorrect mana regeneration (direction not stated) and his passive description; the 24 Sep hotfix review found no reviewed Valmont advice depending on either. The whole 1.17 line is 50.4% over 1354 Gold+ midlane games [47.7, 53.0]; Bronze+ 53.3% over 3593 is nested. His job is a grounding, slowing bind that sets up spell follow-up and survives through Exsanguinate, with no escape. B (situational or practiced) fits a near-even new hero; the reviewed 2.32 plan is spell-focused and avoids the attack-speed text (Bloodbound, Arterial Grip) that the official launch notes and the current source still dispute. Not A: near-even results, no dash, and the midlane S and A options cover control and ranged pressure with fewer conditions. Not C: a large near-even sample and a distinct job (the only Ground source in the 1.17 kits).
entries.limitation: First grade on five days of a new hero's data; ban pressure and learning can still move it. The disputed attack-speed values are not used in the text. Not applied: the packet validator requires a reviewed plan in reviewed_guidance.json, and his midlane plan is in the patch-1.17.json supplement. Applying it needs that plan brought into the packet (or the rule widened), which is outside a grade recheck.

entries.watch: His 1.16.4 samples and his 1.17 jungle results sit below even, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.
entries.reason: B retained. The 2.34 trigger for C was a larger Gold+ sample whose interval excludes the 1.16.4 review rate (48.9% over 2006). The whole 1.17 line is 47.4% over 559 [43.3, 51.6], which includes it, and the 364 games since the review ran 50.0%, so the early drop (42.6% over 195) has partly recovered. No kit reason points either way beyond the sword-pickup fix. Bronze+ 48.2% over 1036 is nested. Watch updated: it said the early 1.17 jungle result was lower still.
entries.limitation: Still below even; if the whole-line interval comes to exclude 48.9%, C remains the candidate.

entries.why: L.I.N.X and Final Thread offer a deliberate spell sequence, with Data Burst supporting the next empowered tool.
